args.decision: Which change should be recommended first to fix the dark, shadowed look of the Gran Turismo cars in the dealership viewer?
args.evidence:
Measurements on Gran Turismo PS1 car GLBs in a three.js r182 viewer (double-sided MeshStandardMaterial, hemisphere ground 0x1a1c20, key+rim lights, no environment, no tone mapping).
Winding: current exporter agreement median 0.144 (727/728 cars below half, day/night/arcade alike). Drop-swap median 0.842. Per-triangle-from-normals median 1.0.
Stored normals: median 16.8% of day-car body area has normals nearly perpendicular to the face (75% of it flat black faces). Repair (geometric normal for those faces) leaves max 1.3%.
Renders, mean car luma current->per_triangle->repaired(base lights)->repaired+env: HNSXN 38.9->89.5->89.5->110.0; NR33N 50.5->105.6->105.6->135.5; CCRVN 24.7->47.6->48.2->52.4; LD7VR 40.4->78.7->81.9->106.2. LD7VR door panel stays blue/dark with per_triangle; uniform with repaired. Unlit rendering gives HNSXN 101.8, NR33N 127.1, CCRVN 47.3, LD7VR 97.6.
Removing flat black faces changes <=0.23% of visible car pixels. Textured faces are raw-texture (unlit) on PS1 hardware. Exporter change requires regenerating GT source GLBs and dealership copies (catalog hashes change).
args.priorities: Fix the shadowed look on every GT car; keep native data provenance; deterministic and verifiable by script; do not tune lighting to hide geometry defects; smallest change that fully fixes the defect.

candidates.description: Exporter: per-face orientation from stored normals, and replace near-perpendicular stored normals with geometric face normals; regenerate GT GLBs and dealership copies.
Exporter: remove the index swap only; regenerate.
Viewer: unlit native display mode for GT cars only; no exporter change.
Viewer: environment map, brighter ground bounce and neutral tone mapping; no exporter change.
Capture an emulator reference of GT1 car rendering before changing anything.

requirements: Corrects the inverted lighting on all 728 cars
Leaves no faces shaded by arbitrary in-plane normals
Keeps lit (PBR) rendering usable in the viewer
